title: Add econ-orchestrator CLI and workload stitcher for automated batching/cache/quant suggestions
author: Maya Chen
description: Summary: Introduces a new CLI tool (redwood econ-orchestrator) and an accompanying workload stitcher pipeline to automate tenant-level batching, cache presets, and quantization profile recommendations. Motivation: customers repeatedly ask for a safe, reproducible way to generate defaults that balance latency SLOs and unit economics without manual trial-and-error. This change packages our simulation + telemetry heuristics into a developer-friendly CLI, supports presets-as-code output, and wires a safety gate that prevents aggressive profiles from being auto-applied. Key features: - redwood econ-orchestrator CLI: local dry-run mode, tenant mode (pulls anonymized telemetry snapshot), and export mode (profiles as YAML). - Workload stitcher: synthesizes realistic batch/sequence-length traces by combining sampled production requests, synthetic tail-length injections, and configurable burst patterns for stress testing. - Econ engine: unit-econ calculator that simulates per-token cost, estimated GPU seconds, and predicted p50/p95 latency under different batch/cache/quant combinations. Produces ranked candidate profiles. - Safety/guardrails: conservative candidate scorer, rollback hints, and a quarantine policy for any profile that increases 95th percentile latency by more than configured threshold. - Profiles-as-code export: YAML artifacts include batching shape, cache TTL hints, quantization target (bits, calibration dataset tag), and human-readable notes. - Integration points: CLI can call the new /internal/econ/simulate endpoint (server-side) or run fully offline using historic telemetry exports. Checklist: - [x] CLI binary and help docs - [x] Workload stitcher library (unit-tested) - [x] Econ simulation module with cost model - [x] Profiles-as-code YAML serializer - [x] Safety scorer and policy enforcement tests - [x] Integration tests exercising server simulate endpoint - [x] E2E smoke with small tenant dataset - [x] Documentation in docs/cost-automation.md (quickstart)

human_summary: This PR delivers a self-contained CLI and library to automate conservative, auditable cost-optimization recommendations. It bundles simulation primitives, a unit-economics model, and guardrails so platform engineers can generate safe defaults for batching, cache TTLs, and quant profiles before applying them to tenants.
